title: Rust: Closures
description: Use closures (anonymous functions) that can capture their environment.

steps.title: Basic Closure
steps.description: Create a closure `let square = |x: i32| x * x;` and call it with 5. Print the result.

verification.failureMessage: Create and call a closure that squares a number.

steps.title: Capturing Environment
steps.description: Create a variable `factor = 3` outside a closure. The closure `|x| x * factor` captures factor by reference. Call it with 10 and print 30.
hints: Closures can capture variables from their surrounding scope.

verification.failureMessage: Create a closure that captures 'factor' and prints 10*factor.

steps.title: Closure as Function Parameter
steps.description: Write a function `apply<F>(x: i32, f: F) -> i32 where F: Fn(i32) -> i32` that applies the closure. Test with `|x| x + 1` and `|x| x * 2`.
hints: `fn apply<F: Fn(i32) -> i32>(x: i32, f: F) -> i32 { f(x) }`

verification.failureMessage: Apply different closures to 5 and print results.

steps.title: FnMut Closure
steps.description: Create a mutable counter using a closure that captures `&mut count`. The closure increments count each time it's called. Call it 3 times and print the counter value.
hints: `let mut count = 0; let mut inc = || { count += 1; count };`
A closure that mutates captured variables implements `FnMut`.

verification.failureMessage: Call a mutable closure 3 times and print the final count.

steps.title: Iterator with Closures
steps.description: Use closures with iterator methods: given `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, filter even numbers with a closure, then map to squares with another closure. Collect and print.

verification.failureMessage: Filter evens and map to squares, print [4, 16].
